Skillet test   Your skills, everywhere.

Usage
  skillet             first run: connect, then sync
  skillet <command>   run any command below

Getting started
  init                  Install the /skillet router skill into your agents. No account needed
  connect <code>        Link this machine with a pair code from skillet.md Settings
  web [path]            Open skillet.md in your browser (e.g. /settings)

Skills into your kit
  create <name>         Start a new skill: scaffold SKILL.md and its eval
  add [source]          Add a skill or kit from the library, GitHub, or a path
  search <keyword...>   Search the public skill library
  list                  List skills grouped by kit

Sync & share
  sync                  Put your kit into every agent on this machine
  mcp                   Serve your kit to MCP agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code)
  upload                Upload local skills, private, to your account
  export <ref>          Export a skill or kit as a .zip for anywhere Skillet cannot sync

This machine
  whoami                Who this machine is signed in as
  logout                Sign out of this machine
  usage                 Skill stats on this machine (local only)
  activity              What Skillet records: view, export, delete, or change it
  device                Your machines: which one this is, plus how to rename it
  doctor                Auth, sync state, pending updates, and paths

More commands   import · eval · scan · pending · edits · trust · pin
Details         skillet <command> --help

# sync
skillet sync   Put your kit into every agent on this machine

Usage
  skillet sync [options]

Options
  --cwd <dir>           Working directory for skillet.lock
  --json                Emit a machine-readable result report
  --dry-run             Preview sync targets and detected agents without writing anything
  --allow-quarantined   Pre-approve quarantined versions in runs without a terminal
  --check               Detect registry changes without writing to agents
  --background          Mark this run as an automatic background sync. Agent folders that still need macOS folder access stay parked
  --user-initiated      Mark this run as user-initiated. Skillet may read agent folders that require a macOS folder-access prompt, and remembers the grant
  --token <token>       Bearer token (session, device, or env override)
  -h, --help            display help for command

# activity
activity   What Skillet records: view, export, delete, or change it

Usage
  skillet activity <command> [options]

Commands
  status [options]          Show whether activity is recorded and what decides it
  on                        Turn activity recording on
  off                       Turn activity recording off (opt out)
  choose [options] <where>  Answer the skill-stats question: `sync` stats to your account, or keep them `local`
  clear                     Delete your recorded activity: local history and server events
  export                    Export everything recorded about you (local route history + server activity)

Options
  -h, --help
    display help for command

Run `skillet activity <command> --help` for command-specific options.

# edits
edits   Skills you customized: your live edits, with author updates held

Usage
  skillet edits <command> [options]

Commands
  list [options]             List your customized skills and which have a held update
  check [options]            Detect unreconciled local edits (read-only; for the desktop tray)
  diff [options] <skill>     Show your version against the author's current one
  take <skill>               Replace your edit with the author's version (backs yours up first)
  restore <skill>            Replace your edit with the author's original (backs yours up first)
  keep <skill>               Acknowledge a held update so it stops nudging until the next one
  propose [options] <skill>  Propose your edit upstream to the skill's author

Options
  -h, --help
    display help for command

Run `skillet edits <command> --help` for command-specific options.

# add
add   Add a skill or kit from the library, GitHub, or a path

Usage
  skillet add <command> [options]

Commands
  kit [options] <ref>  Subscribe to a kit and sync its skills

Options
  --registry <url>
    Registry base URL
  --ref <ref>
    GitHub branch, tag, or commit
  --skill <name>
    Install only the named skill(s) from a repo; repeatable
  --list
    List discoverable skills without installing
  -y, --yes
    Skip prompts; use defaults
  -g, --global
    Install only to Universal ~/.agents/skills (skip other agents)
  -a, --adapter <name>
    Target agent(s) by name; repeatable
  --json
    Machine-readable output
  --token <token>
    Bearer token override
  --pin
    Pin registry skill to current version
  --cwd <dir>
    Working directory for skillet.lock
  -h, --help
    display help for command

Run `skillet add <command> --help` for command-specific options.

# add kit
skillet add kit   Subscribe to a kit and sync its skills

Usage
  skillet add kit [options] <ref>

Options
  --registry <url>      Registry base URL
  --ref <ref>           GitHub branch, tag, or commit
  --skill <name>        Install only the named skill(s) from a repo; repeatable
  --list                List discoverable skills without installing
  -y, --yes             Skip prompts; use defaults
  -g, --global          Install only to Universal ~/.agents/skills (skip other agents)
  -a, --adapter <name>  Target agent(s) by name; repeatable
  --json                Machine-readable output
  --token <token>       Bearer token override
  --pin                 Pin registry skill to current version
  --cwd <dir>           Working directory for skillet.lock
  -h, --help            display help for command

Arguments
  ref  


# import
skillet import   Bring skills you already have (in your agents or a folder) into your kit

Usage
  skillet import [options] [source]

Options
  -y, --yes             Import every discovered skill without prompting
  --ref <ref>           GitHub branch, tag, or commit to import from
  --skill <name>        Import only the named skill(s) from a repo; repeatable. Skips the picker.
  --all                 Import every skill found in the repo; skips the picker
  --force               Overwrite an existing kit skill when the slug collides
  --local               Import into your kit only; don't back up to your account
  -h, --help            display help for command

Arguments
  source

# upload
skillet upload   Upload local skills, private, to your account

Usage
  skillet upload [options] [name]

Options
  --skill <slug>        Upload only the named skill(s); repeatable
  --all                 Upload every un-published local skill (required for a no --skill batch)
  --public              Publish publicly (requires confirmation; default is private)
  --yes                 Skip the public-upload confirmation (required for --public without a terminal)
  --json                Emit a machine-readable report (for the desktop app)
  --registry <url>      Registry base URL
  --token <token>       Session token (defaults to $SKILLET_TOKEN)
  -h, --help            display help for command

Arguments
  name  


# mcp
skillet mcp   Serve your kit to MCP agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code)

Usage
  skillet mcp [options]

Options
  --port <number>       Start HTTP transport on this port instead of stdio
  --token <token>       Bearer token for stdio mode (defaults to this machine's paired device token)
  -h, --help            display help for command



Overview
  Expose your local Skillet kit to MCP clients that run on this machine:
  Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, or any client that can spawn a local
  MCP server. The server is a read-only view over ~/.skillet/skills/, skills
  you already synced and approved.

Before you start
  Run skillet sync (or sync from the desktop app) so ~/.skillet/skills/ has
  content.

Transports
  stdio (default): local subprocess clients spawn skillet mcp and talk over
    stdin/stdout. Use for Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Claude Code.
  HTTP (--port <n>): loopback Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1 for local HTTP
    clients. On start, a loopback bearer is saved to
    ~/.skillet/mcp-loopback-token (mode 0600).

Auth
  stdio: uses this machine's paired device token automatically (device.json,
    falling back to your session). Pass --token to override with a skillet_s_
    (session), skillet_d_ (device), or skillet_k_ (kit key) bearer. An
    unpaired machine with no token serves an empty skill list (fail-closed).
  HTTP: every request must present the loopback bearer from
    ~/.skillet/mcp-loopback-token or a registry-validated skillet bearer as
    Authorization: Bearer …. Prefix-only tokens are rejected.

Tools
  list_skills()     Kit manifest (slug, name, description, version, author)
  get_skill(slug)   SKILL.md body plus supporting-file resource URIs
  search_skills(q)  Keyword search over name and description

Resources
  skillet://{owner}/{slug}/{path}   one resource per file in each skill bundle
  (e.g. skillet://you/my-skill/SKILL.md). Owner _local for unowned imports.

Examples

  Claude Desktop / Cursor (claude_desktop_config.json or ~/.cursor/mcp.json):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "skillet": {
          "command": "skillet",
          "args": ["mcp"]
        }
      }
    }

  HTTP loopback (local HTTP clients on this machine):

    skillet mcp --port 8765
    # Point the client at http://127.0.0.1:8765 with:
    # Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.skillet/mcp-loopback-token)

Web agents (ChatGPT, Claude.ai)
  These run in the cloud and cannot reach a server on your machine. Connect
  them with your hosted MCP link instead: on https://skillet.md, open Settings → Account,
  turn on MCP, and paste the link into the client. (skillet export + bundle
  upload still works as a static snapshot alternative.)

More
  https://skillet.md/docs/mcp
  https://skillet.md/docs/runtimes/claude-ai
  https://skillet.md/docs/runtimes/chatgpt
  Run skillet export for a static .zip when a client cannot use MCP.

# route
route   The /skillet router: picks the right skill for a task

Usage
  skillet route <command> [options]

Commands
  manifest [options]            List kit skills for agent routing (metadata only, no SKILL.md bodies)
  begin [options]               Record a /skillet invocation (metadata only)
  hook [options]                Agent hook entrypoint for /skillet
  record [options] <skill-ref>  Record a routed skill pick
  help [command]                display help for command

Options
  -h, --help
    display help for command

Run `skillet route <command> --help` for command-specific options.

# route manifest
skillet route manifest   List kit skills for agent routing (metadata only, no SKILL.md bodies)

Usage
  skillet route manifest [options]

Options
  --json                Emit machine-readable manifest
  -h, --help            display help for command


# route begin
skillet route begin   Record a /skillet invocation (metadata only)

Usage
  skillet route begin [options]

Options
  --runtime <runtime>   Agent name, e.g. cursor
  --source <source>     Recorder source, e.g. cursor-hook
  --surface <surface>   Invocation surface, e.g. user-prompt-submit
  --json                Emit machine-readable result
  -h, --help            display help for command


# route hook
skillet route hook   Agent hook entrypoint for /skillet

Usage
  skillet route hook [options]

Options
  --runtime <runtime>   Agent name, e.g. cursor, claude-code, codex
  -h, --help            display help for command
